summary: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories.
takeaways: We evaluate SPLICE across two policy families on two long-horizon agent tasks, Software Engineering with SWE-bench Verified and Deep Research with BrowseComp-Plus.
Further experiments show that SPLICE improves performance while reducing costly proposal-model computation.
A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories.
